mentl/aeda6c2:
Closes Stage 4b of the cargo-class multi-core cascade. The handler IS
the backend (DESIGN Ch 7.3): memory strategy IS a handler swap. With
this handler installed in the ~> chain, every allocation uses
i32.atomic.rmw.cmpxchg on a memory-resident heap pointer at address
0x40 (clear of WASI scratch [0x50, 0x250)).

Substrate:

  handler emit_memory_atomic_cas {
    emit_alloc(size, target) => {
      // CAS loop: read heap_ptr@0x40, compute next, cmpxchg.
      // br_if exits when witness == expected (we won the race).
      // Multiple threads can allocate concurrently without lock.
      ...
    }
  }

The substrate is a pure swap surface — installing
`~> emit_memory_atomic_cas` instead of `~> emit_memory_bump` produces
WAT that's lock-free thread-safe. Programs that don't install
parallel_compose use the existing bump handler with zero runtime
overhead.

Peer follow-up `Hβ.emit.cas-alloc-init-in-start` — _start preamble
to initialize heap_ptr@0x40 = 0x100000 (1 MiB) before any allocation.
The swap surface IS the substrate; the init bridge is one named
peer.

The cargo-class multi-core cascade is now substrate-complete:
- Stage 1: bootstrap shared memory + wasi thread-spawn import ✓
- Stage 2: wheel emit_memory_decl shared memory + import ✓
- Stage 3: closure-IS-thread-record collapse (threading.mn + emit) ✓
- Stage 4a: LWasiCall direct-import bridge ✓
- Stage 4b: lock-free atomic CAS bump allocator handler ✓

Activation post-L1:
1. mentl2 self-compiles wheel → mentl3.wat
2. mentl3.wat installs `~> emit_memory_atomic_cas` in its ~> chain
   (via main.mn or pipeline.mn handler-chain edit)
3. wasmtime run -W threads=y -W shared-memory=y -S threads=y mentl3.wasm
4. parallel_compose dispatches N branches to N OS threads via
   $wasi_thread_spawn; each thread's allocations CAS-claim from
   shared heap; ffi_join atomic-waits on closure_done_addr until
   thread sets done=1; result reads from closure_result_addr.

Cores light up. The substrate IS the work.

stoop/aea1ad9:
The chrome was a dark terminal with orange Courier on it and the pages
floated on it as white islands. A tool for making photocopied paper
should be made of the same stuff: off-white stock with a faint grain,
black ink, and one riso fluoro pink where a thing wants pressing. The
drawers are paper slid over paper with a shadow, not a blackout. The
colour tokens were renamed first, because a token called night that
means off-white is a lie left for the next reader: bg, bg2, fg, spot,
link. The hand kit in press/ keeps its own stylesheet and its own dark.

On a phone the page comes first. The tools sit on a bar along the bottom
where a thumb is, the nav is one scrolling row instead of three wrapped
ones, and a drawer takes the whole width. Those rules load last, in
their own file, so they win over the desktop rules in the others; put in
base.css they lost to views.css and the bar wrapped anyway.

The press stopped shouting at a stranger. Its status line told a person
who had just opened a blank press, in red, that the sheet was empty and
they were looking at a draft; it now says nothing until there is a
published issue to be confused with, which is the case it exists for.
